 heads into the final days of October with a dated event on the calendar. According to the company's company website release, the energy major will publish quarterly financial results in October, and management will discuss them on a live call that begins in the morning Central time. The release followed the usual pattern, with the announcement made weeks before the report. Exxon Mobil is among the companies tracked in our Oil and Gas Stocks coverage. The timing matters because Exxon Mobil is among the largest components of the S&P 500, so its quarterly update often sets the tone for the rest of the energy group. Exxon Mobil shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange and are tracked by the S&P 500, NYSE Composite and Russell 1000. Reports from Stock Titan, Defense World and Yahoo Finance all pointed to the same date, and a preview on Yahoo Finance framed the report as a test of how the company's different businesses performed together. This article lays out what is known and what is not. It separates the confirmed schedule from outside expectations, describes the business segments that will be reported, and notes the challenges that management is likely to be asked. No results have been published yet, so no figures from the quarter are cited here. The confirmed facts are narrow but clear. In a press release posted on its company website, Exxon Mobil said it would release quarterly financial results in October. The company added that a live webcast and call would follow in the morning Central time, which is in the morning in New York. The announcement was syndicated by wire services and picked up by Stock Titan and Yahoo Finance, which is how the date reached most market participants. As is typical, the company did not preview any results in the notice. It only provided the date, the time and the instructions for listening to the webcast. Because the call comes after the release of the numbers, stock owners will have the written results first and the explanation second. That sequence often produces a step reaction, with an initial move on the headline figures and a second adjustment as management answers questions about cash flow, project timing and capital spending. Everything else in circulation, including estimates for earnings per share and revenue, comes from outside data providers rather than from Exxon Mobil. Those numbers vary by source and by the time they were compiled, which is why they are treated here as context rather than fact. Exxon Mobil reports through a handful of segments, and the quarter will show how each contributed. The upstream business produces crude oil and natural gas, and its results depend on volumes and realized prices. Energy Products, Chemical Products and Specialty Products, the downstream groupings the company has used in recent filings, depend on refining margins, chemical spreads and demand for lubricants and other specialty goods. This mix is what distinguishes the company from many exploration and production peers. When crude prices fall, refining and chemical margins can sometimes offset part of the weakness, and the reverse can also happen. The quarterly report is the moment when that internal balance becomes visible. Corporate costs and financing charges round out the picture. The company has repeatedly said that it is working to lower its structural cost base, and the quarter will show how much of that effort is appearing in reported numbers rather than in presentations. For readers following the stock, the segment table in the earnings release is usually more informative than the single headline figure. A strong total can mask weakness in part of the portfolio, and a soft total can hide a business that is moving in the right direction. Growth areas have dominated the company's communications in recent years. The first is the Permian Basin in West Texas and New Mexico, which expanded after the company completed its acquisition of Pioneer Natural Resources. The second is offshore Guyana, where Exxon Mobil operates the Stabroek Block with partners and has brought several floating production vessels online. Market participants usually look for things in these regions. Is whether volumes are meeting the company's stated plans. The other is whether per-barrel costs are improving as the Permian operation is integrated and as more Guyana capacity ramps up. Both are visible in the production tables and in management commentary. Liquefied natural gas is another area to watch. The company has long-term projects under way, including a Texas export terminal in which it participates with partners, and the timing of start-up affects when volumes begin to contribute to results. Delays or early completions can shift the earnings pattern quarter to the next. The company has not said, in the materials reviewed for this article, how the quarter compares with the second on any of these measures. That comparison will arrive and it is the first thing Wall Street research desks will update in their models. Refining margins, often called crack spreads, measure the gap between the price of crude oil and the price of the fuels made from it. They tend to be strong when inventories are tight or when unplanned outages remove supply, and weak when demand softens or product stocks build. The quarter includes the end of the summer driving season, which normally supports gasoline and diesel demand. Chemicals are a different story. Margins in that business have been under pressure across the industry because of new capacity in Asia and uneven demand in construction and manufacturing. Exxon Mobil has argued that its integrated sites and its focus on higher-value products give it an advantage, and the report will show whether that claim is visible in the numbers. Planned maintenance is another variable. Refineries frequently schedule turnarounds in the shoulder months, and these can reduce throughput and raise costs for a quarter. The company usually flags such effects in its release or on the call, and they help explain why quarter looks unlike the last. None of these inputs can be read from the calendar announcement. They are described here because they are the factors that will explain the downstream line when it is published, and because they have been decisive in prior quarters according to the company's own filings. Crude oil prices have been volatile this year, moved by shifting demand expectations, decisions by large producing nations and headlines about supply routes in the Middle East. Coverage of other U.S. producers in recent weeks has referred to supply concerns around the Strait of Hormuz as factor supporting prices at times. For an integrated major, higher crude prices lift upstream earnings quickly, while the downstream businesses may face higher feedstock costs that arrive with a lag. The company has said in previous quarterly materials that it publishes sensitivity information to help readers estimate these effects, and that disclosure is useful for interpreting the quarter. Natural gas prices matter as well. A move in either direction changes line of the earnings statement, which is why the company's reconciliations of earnings by factor are closely read. Geopolitics also affects costs and logistics. Sanctions, shipping disruptions and regional conflicts can alter trade flows and insurance expenses. The company typically addresses these topics only in general terms, and market participants will listen for any change in tone. Cash allocation is a recurring theme for Exxon Mobil. The company's stated order of priorities has been to fund its capital program, support the dividend, keep a strong balance sheet and then use surplus cash for a share retirement program. How much of each it can afford depends on operating cash flow, which in turn depends on commodity prices and downstream margins. The dividend is closely watched because the company has raised it for many consecutive years, a record that stock owners regard as a signal of confidence in durable cash generation. The quarterly report is not the usual time for a dividend change, since the company has tended to announce those in other quarters, but the declaration and any commentary on the payout are part of the package. Capital spending is the other side of the ledger. Management has described a multi-year plan that emphasizes projects with strong expected economics, and it has said it will adjust the pace if conditions change. The report and call should show whether spending is tracking the plan or moving away from it. Net debt and the balance sheet round out the picture. Exxon Mobil entered recent quarters with low leverage by industry standards, and lenders will want to see that remain the case after the Pioneer deal and ongoing project spending. The energy group enters reporting season with a mixed pattern. Some pure exploration and production companies have seen their shares reach new multi-month highs in October, according to market data sites, while integrated majors have moved more modestly. The difference reflects the way each business model responds to crude oil prices. Exxon Mobil's scale gives it a different profile from smaller producers. It has a larger refining and chemical system, a bigger project pipeline and a balance sheet built to carry through cycles. That also means that its quarterly numbers tend to change less sharply than those of a company that produces only crude oil and gas. Chevron, Shell, BP and TotalEnergies report around the same time, and comparisons across the group are common. Differences in accounting for timing effects, divestments and non-recurring items can make direct comparisons tricky, so the company's own breakdown of identified items is the safer starting point. Index funds that track the S&P 500 or the [Dow Jones Industrial Average] also own the stock, so its result feeds into the broader energy weighting even though that weighting is small next to technology. Commodity price swings are the most obvious uncertainty. A quarter that begins with level for crude oil and ends with another can leave results that look different from what a simple average would imply, especially when hedging, inventory accounting and timing effects are involved. Project execution is a second challenge. Large offshore and export projects can be delayed by weather, supply chain bottlenecks or regulatory approvals, and the company has historically been candid about adjusting timelines. Any change in start-up schedules for major developments would be a notable item in the report. Climate-related disclosure rules, state and local legal actions and changes in environmental permitting all carry costs and can affect strategy. The company discusses these in its annual and quarterly filings, and the legal proceedings section is where updates appear. Finally, demand uncertainty persists. Economic growth rates, electric vehicle adoption and efficiency gains all influence long-term consumption of oil products, and the pace of change is debated. Management commentary on demand is typically cautious, which gives balance to the more optimistic production figures. The stock has not always moved in line with the headline result. In some earlier quarters, shares rose on a beat and then faded as the call revealed higher spending or softer chemical margins. In others, a modest miss was overshadowed by strong production or a confident message about costs. Market participants therefore often focus on earnings excluding identified items, and on cash flow from operations, rather than the reported net figure. Options pricing and trading volume usually rise ahead of the report, which can amplify the first reaction. A calm market on the day does not mean the report was unimportant, only that it matched what had been built into the price. That can produce a second round of repricing depending on how the details are interpreted and on what the rest of the sector reports in the days that follow. The first item is the earnings release itself, which will include the segment table, the cash flow summary and the list of identified items. The company also files a quarterly report with the Securities and Exchange Commission, usually within days, and that document contains the legal and accounting detail. The second item is the live call in the morning Central time. Management typically walks through the quarter, discusses progress on major projects and takes questions. Comments on production growth, cost reductions and capital spending are the ones most likely to change expectations. Those updates reflect their own judgments and are not company statements, so they should be read as commentary rather than as confirmed information. Finally, the reports from other energy companies over the next weeks, including ConocoPhillips, EOG Resources and Devon Energy, will help show whether Exxon Mobil's results reflect sector-wide conditions or company-specific factors. The calendar is crowded, and the picture will fill in gradually. Jefferies finds BTE's relative valuation "compelling," adding that its growth runway should allow for the shares to re-rate higher. Shares of AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) slipped over 1% in overnight trading late Tuesday as the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) cleared Amazon’s $11.5 billion Globalstar acquisition, pushing the tech giant’s satellite-to-phone ambitions forward and setting the stage for tougher competition. ASTS stock jumped 6% on Tuesday to $41.96, but shares are still down 29% for the month. The FCC’s Space Bureau approved the transaction on Tuesday, including the transfer of 25 megahertz of Globalstar’s internationally harmonized mobile-satellite spectrum.  “This will enhance Amazon’s offering of direct-to-device (D2D) services, which will mean even more competition, coverage, and capacity,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said on X. The deal will pair Amazon Leo’s satellite-building capabilities, launch arrangements and ground infrastructure with Globalstar’s existing network and spectrum. The spectrum is key to Amazon’s satellite-to-phone ambitions. In its approval order, the FCC said Amazon has applied to operate a global direct-to-device system but would lack the mobile-satellite spectrum needed to run it without the acquisition. Amazon plans to use Globalstar’s assets to expand capacity and bring more services to areas beyond cellular coverage. The FCC said the deal could help close coverage gaps, boost emergency communications and improve data services for businesses and industrial users. “By approving this deal, the FCC has empowered Amazon Leo to deliver fast, next-gen satellite broadband services, increase competition, and help communities stay connected all across the country,” Carr said in the announcement. The FCC’s review also highlights how the deal could strengthen a rival to AST SpaceMobile. In its approval order, the agency cited arguments from Public Knowledge and New America’s Open Technology Institute that combining Amazon’s resources with Globalstar’s assets could create a stronger competitor to SpaceX and T-Mobile’s satellite offering, as well as AST’s partnership with AT&T. The order also notes AST’s ties with Verizon and FirstNet. AST already has FCC authorization to deploy and operate up to 248 satellites, connecting directly to standard smartphones using 700 MHz and 800 MHz spectrum in coordination with AT&T, Verizon and FirstNet. Its commercial agreement with AT&T, announced in 2024, runs through 2030. AST also signed a definitive agreement with Verizon last year. Amazon is targeting a similar opportunity: helping mobile carriers extend voice, text and data services beyond the reach of cellular towers. The company plans to begin deploying its next-generation satellite-to-device system in 2028. The deal would bring Amazon an established Apple relationship, with Globalstar already supporting emergency messaging and location sharing on compatible iPhones and Apple Watches. Amazon and Apple have agreed to maintain those services and develop future satellite features through Amazon Leo. Amazon also aims to expand beyond Globalstar’s current offerings to serve more carriers and device makers. The acquisition is expected to close in 2027, subject to remaining conditions, including replacement-satellite milestones. Amazon’s separate application for its direct-to-device system remains pending. After closing, it could also use Globalstar’s U.S. market-access approval for the planned 48-satellite C-3 network. Meanwhile, the FCC’s meeting on Thursday could advance a spectrum auction and proposals to open 500 megahertz of additional spectrum for uses including satellite-to-device services. (BA) stock is heading for a weekly loss as CEO Robert Ortberg outlined a path to $10 billion in free cash flow by 2029, with the company’s 737 production stabilization taking longer than expected. Boeing expects to reach its target production rate of 47 jets monthly in 2027, with cash flow improving over the next three years. Boeing stock edged up 0.2% overnight Tuesday after a 10% drop in regular trading. During the third-quarter (Q3) earnings call, Ortberg said Boeing is working to establish a manufacturing pace of 47 737 aircraft per month and needs additional time to sustain its targeted production rate. “On 737, we continue to work towards stabilizing production at 47 airplanes per month. Our factory key performance indicators are performing well, particularly in the final assembly, where we've seen a 40% improvement in rework since the start of last year. However, as I mentioned at a conference last month, it is taking us longer than we had expected to demonstrate performance at rate 47. We're making progress, but we still have more work to do, and I'm expecting it will take us into next year to get fully stable at this rate.” Boeing received U.S. approval last week for the 737 Max 10, its largest model in the 737 Max family, after a six-year wait. The plane has over 1,550 orders, making up more than 30% of Boeing’s total 737 Max orders. The delay followed safety checks after two deadly 737 Max 8 crashes in 2018 and 2019. Ortberg acknowledged that shareholders have struggled to predict how Boeing’s operational improvements would translate into the balance sheet. The company expects to generate roughly $2 billion in free cash flow in 2026, followed by approximately $3 billion in 2027. That 2027 outlook includes additional capital spending to develop the F/A-XX program, the U.S. Navy’s sixth-generation fighter jet contract. Boeing expects free cash flow to rise to about $6 billion in 2028 before reaching its $10 billion goal in 2029. Ortberg expects the financial recovery to pick up as some existing pressures ease. The 777X program will remain a drag in the near term. “With respect to program cash flow, we continue to expect 2027 to be a significant use of cash with 2028 improving before turning positive in 2029,” said CFO Jesus Malave of the 777X. Jefferies called Boeing’s free cash flow targets “disappointing,” noting that each year’s goal had slipped by about a year. title: America’s Emergency Oil Reserve Is at a 1982 Low, and Gas Is Costlier Than Under Biden - 24/7 Wall St.
content: America's emergency oil cushion is draining at a pace not seen since the early 1980s, and drivers are quietly crossing a threshold that carries serious political consequences for the White House heading into the midterms. America’s emergency oil stockpile and its gasoline bill each crossed a political line on October 26, 2026. The Energy Department reported that Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude stocks fell to 282.6 million barrels, the lowest since October 1982. AAA data showed regular gasoline has averaged $3.472 a gallon during Trump’s current term, compared with $3.471 under Biden. Crude moved little, as Brent settled down 91 cents, or 0.8%, at $115.81 a barrel, and WTI fell $1.51, or 1.46%, to $101.76. United States Oil Fund (NYSEARCA:USO) slid 1.97% to $166.19. State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (NYSEARCA:XLE) rose 0.43% to $69.63. The Finland-based Center for Research on Energy and Clean Air, an advocacy nonprofit that wants countries to move off fossil fuels, estimates US consumers have paid an extra $471 each for fuel since the Iran war began February 28. The worldwide figure is about $60 per person. Americans account for $160 billion of the $468 billion in extra spending across the 169 countries studied. The reserve is there to cover supply shocks, so its size tells traders how much buffer Washington has left. The drop comes from a committed withdrawal of 172 million barrels. On top of that, the department approved an emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels to cover a disruption at Phillips 66 (NYSE:PSX | PSX Price Prediction) in Lake Charles, Louisiana. The reserve held 415.442 million barrels in the week ending March 6 and 282.683 million barrels in the week ending October 16. That is a drop of about 133 million barrels, or roughly 32%, in about seven months. The last time the level was lower was the week ending October 15, 1982, at 280.802 million barrels. The reserve actually grew under Trump at first, from 394.566 million barrels in January 2025, until the war release began. Because less oil is left to soften the next shock, traders are likely to keep paying extra for crude. Last week, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia intensified, stoking fears about energy security and infrastructure and shipments across the Middle East. UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo also reportedly told Reuters that any further escalation could trigger renewed supply disruptions. Brett Erickson, Managing Principal at Obsidian Risk Advisors, said in a post on X over the weekend, “Iran is currently launching missiles and drones at vessels attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the preparations from all sides to ready for a full-scale resumption of the war, Iran does not intend to allow the U.S. to use this window to flow out excessive amount of oil and refined products in the meantime.” Exxon Mobil, ConocoPhillips and Chevron surged to 52-week highs on Friday amid the steep climb in oil prices. XOM stock hit a 52-week high of $183.75 during trading hours on Friday, closing nearly 3% higher. Shares of AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) slipped 0.4% overnight late Sunday even as the company sought more spectrum to expand its satellite broadband capabilities, while market veteran Herb Greenberg questioned its valuation despite a steep selloff. ASTS stock jumped nearly 3% on Friday to close at $39.70, but ended the week down 2%, marking its fourth consecutive weekly decline. In a Friday statement, AST’s unit, AST & Science, proposed adding Q/V and E-band service-link capabilities to its 248-satellite network. The links would connect satellites directly to customer terminals, broadening its proposed high-frequency operations beyond ground-gateway connections. The request covers selected frequencies between 40 and 51.4 GHz, plus downlinks at 71 GHz -74 GHz and uplinks at 81GHz –84 GHz.  “This supports a deployment model in which the smallest terminal classes can be used by functional mobile user equipment with varying bandwidths, powers, and antenna sizes,” AST said. The proposed services would require compatible terminals alongside AST’s core connectivity offering for standard smartphones. “AST SpaceMobile’s operations are not solely dependent on use of the E-band; AST SpaceMobile will utilize other spectrum, including the Q/V-band and 700/800 MHz bands, for its user terminals in addition to the E-band spectrum,” the filing said. Approval and interference coordination are still necessary, including protections for military users in certain bands. Meanwhile, Greenberg, a veteran financial journalist and investment researcher, questioned AST’s realistic profit potential despite its expanding addressable market. He noted that shares had lost over half their value over six months and recently hit a 52-week low. “Even with that, it’s still priced as if it’s the hottest thing ever, especially when compared with its more established Satcom peers,” he said. Greenberg highlighted an enterprise valuation of 140 times trailing revenue, versus 38 times for Globalstar, 7.5 times for Iridium and three times for Viasat. He also noted a trailing EBITDA loss of about $532 million. “Drilling deeper, based on trailing multiples, you wouldn’t know that its network is nowhere near fully built out yet,” he said. He highlighted multiples of 16 times estimated 2028 revenue and 324 times estimated 2028 adjusted EBITDA, based on $1 billion in revenue and $50 million in adjusted EBITDA. Greenberg acknowledged that a “sky-high valuation” alone rarely justifies avoiding or shorting a stock, while highlighting high short interest and Fidelity’s warning of securities-lending stress. AST is targeting initial, intermittent coverage before year-end in the United States, Canada, Japan, the United Kingdom and Saudi Arabia, subject to regulatory approvals. Continuous service will require more satellites. “We are moving toward service with the partnerships, spectrum and network capabilities needed to bring cellular broadband from space into people’s everyday lives,” President Scott Wisniewski said. The company has more than 60 gateways deployed, installed or planned, supporting over 60 mobile operators whose networks reach more than three billion subscribers. It targets 100 MHz of U.S. spectrum access and 5,600 activated coverage cells before year-end, up from over 3,000. Meanwhile, its smartphone-focused network has shown peak downloads of 98.9 Mbps, with next-gen satellites expected to reach about 200 Mbps. In Europe, Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefonica and Vodafone are exploring a joint mobile-satellite spectrum bid, with a satellite provider yet to be selected. On the other hand, Viasat has challenged an earlier AST overseas-spectrum application as “fatally flawed” over interference and allocation concerns. Biotech stocks enter the week following strong gains, with investor attention turning to Eli Lilly and Merck’s earnings, Oruka Therapeutics’ psoriasis readout and three approaching FDA deadlines. Healthcare and biotech stocks outperformed the broader market in the week ended Oct. 23. The Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLV) rose 1.5%, while the iShares Biotechnology ETF (IBB) gained 2.9% and the SPDR S&P Biotech ETF (XBI) climbed 3.6%. By comparison, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) fell 0.4%, and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) declined 0.8%. Oruka Therapeutics (ORKA) opens Monday with 16-week results from Everlast-B, its Phase 2b trial of Orka-001 in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. The long-acting IL-23 antibody is being developed for less frequent dosing. In the earlier Phase 2a Everlast-A trial, 63.5% of treated patients achieved completely clear skin at Week 16, rising to 71.4% at Week 28 after doses only at Weeks 0 and 4. Incyte (INCY) follows with an investor webcast on its ESMO cancer findings and pipeline. Highlights include INCB161734, which targets the KRAS G12D cancer mutation in colorectal and pancreatic cancers, and dual-target antibody INCA33890. The findings come from early-stage studies, with separate Phase 3 trials underway. ESMO Congress continues through Tuesday in Madrid. Iovance Biotherapeutics (IOVA) presents Monday on Lifileucel, which uses patients’ own immune cells to fight cancer, in two previously treated soft-tissue sarcomas. The data come from a Memorial Sloan Kettering-led pilot trial. Summit Therapeutics (SMMT) enters the week after reporting positive Harmoni-GI1 results on Sunday. In the China-based Phase 3 trial, Ivonescimab plus chemotherapy reduced the risk of death by 25% compared with Durvalumab plus chemotherapy in advanced biliary tract cancer. Median overall survival was 14.9 months versus 12.1 months at the interim analysis. Novartis (NVS) reports Tuesday, followed by Biogen (BIIB) and GSK on Wednesday. Thursday’s lineup includes Eli Lilly (LLY), Merck (MRK), Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY) and Gilead Sciences (GILD), which reports after the market closes. AbbVie (ABBV), AstraZeneca (AZN), Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (REGN) and Sanofi (SNY) follow on Friday. Lilly’s results will test momentum in its diabetes and obesity business after Mounjaro and Zepbound helped drive second-quarter growth and the company raised its full-year revenue outlook. GSK reports after the recent FDA approval of Hibsago, or Bepirovirsen, its Ionis-partnered chronic hepatitis B treatment. Beam Therapeutics (BEAM) reviews initial Phase 1/2 Beam-301 data in glycogen storage disease type Ia on Tuesday. Additionally, Benitec Biopharma (BNTC) will present BB-301 findings at the Oct.27-Oct.30 European Society of Gene and Cell Therapy congress. Inovio (INO) has a Friday target date for INO-3107, a DNA immunotherapy for adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis, which causes recurring airway growths. The company is seeking accelerated approval on a standard FDA review timetable. The FDA previously questioned the application’s eligibility for accelerated approval. In August, Inovio’s said its late-cycle meeting and pre-license inspections were complete, with cash expected to last into late first-quarter 2027. Meanwhile, Agios (AGIO) closes the weekly calendar with a Sunday target date for Mitapivat in sickle cell disease. The application received Priority Review and is seeking accelerated approval based on Phase 2 and Phase 3 Rise Up results. AI ambitions, merger speculation and shifting growth outlooks drove last week’s tech headlines, as SpaceX (SPCX) ramped up chip spending, Nokia Oyj (NOK) and Super Micro Computer (SMCI) benefitted from AI demand, Tesla’s SpaceX merger interest intensified, and Netflix (NFLX) battled fading viewer engagement. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said the company secured a $40 billion financing arrangement to buy advanced AI chips, citing the enormous cost of expanding computing infrastructure. In an X post, that the funding would primarily cover graphics processing units (GPUs). Musk pointed to the company’s investment-grade credit ratings and revenue from Starlink and rocket launches as factors supporting its ability to borrow. SpaceX reported third-quarter revenue of $14.58 billion, up 161% year-on-year. Revenue from its AI business surged nearly tenfold to $7.56 billion. Musk has also set an ambitious outlook, aiming for SpaceX to bring in $1 trillion in annual revenue by 2030. SpaceX stock has gained 1% over the week. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’. Nokia delivered better-than-expected Q3 earnings as demand from AI and cloud customers lifted data center networking sales. Operating profit jumped 35%, and the company kept its 2026 profit forecast unchanged. Despite the upbeat results, Nokia stock plunged over 10% in the week as investors worried it may struggle to turn strong AI orders into sales because of supply shortages, high costs, and reliance on major cloud companies. Rosenblatt lowered its price target on Nokia to $14 from $15 but maintained a ‘Buy’ rating, citing the stock’s post-earnings sell-off was excessive. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’. Super Micro Computer stock gained 4% this week after the company expected Q1 revenue between $18.5 billion and $19.5 billion, above the $15 billion consensus estimate, according to Fiscal.ai. Strong preliminary results reflect rising demand for its AI servers, which use Nvidia chips widely used in modern AI data centers. Super Micro is also working with Nokia and Nvidia to bring AI computing to 5G networks and prepare them for 6G. The company introduced a new server rack powered by Nvidia’s Vera CPUs for AI systems that can plan and perform tasks with limited human help. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘bullish’. Tesla stock rose nearly 5% over the week as the company delivered better-than-expected Q3 earnings. However, Tesla’s capital expenditures rose 110% to $4.7 billion as it leans toward AI and robotics. Investors took note when Musk said merging SpaceX and Tesla would be a good idea. Both companies have formed independent committees to study the proposal, but a deal is not certain. BNP Paribas upgraded Tesla to ‘Neutral’ from ‘Underperform’ and raised its price target to $420 from $266. The analyst said Tesla’s AI progress has been slow, and its heavy spending has increased investment risks. However, the possibility of SpaceX buying Tesla has become a major factor in the firm’s valuation outlook. Netflix stock tumbled 6% during the week as the streaming giant faces slower revenue growth amid rising competition and as it works to attract more viewers and expand its advertising business. Netflix’s Q3 Revenue reached $12.9 billion, in line with expectations, but the company gave a weaker Q4 sales outlook. According to a Bloomberg report, Netflix users are opening the app less often and watching less content, raising concerns about declining viewer interest. Cancellations remain low, but advertising sales are weaker than expected. The company is spending more on shows and movies and adding live sports and podcasts to attract and keep viewers. However, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’. So far this year, while SPCX, TSLA, and NFLX stocks have declined between  8% and 29%, SMCI and NOK stocks have gained 12% and 25%, respectively.
